references.text: The Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord when he displays his glory through Pharaoh and his army
The Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord when he shows his glory through Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen
The Lord promises to deliver the children of Israel from Egypt with a mighty hand and great judgments
The Lord will stretch out his hand and strike Egypt with all his wonders
The Lord stretches out his hand against the nations so that they may know that he is the Lord
Egypt shall know that the Lord is God
The Lord executes judgment on Egypt, and they shall know that he is the Lord
The peoples shall know that the Lord alone is the Most High over all the earth
The Lord raised up Pharaoh to show his power so that his name might be proclaimed throughout the whole earth
The Lord brought the children of Israel out of Egypt
Ezekiel uses the language of the Exodus regarding the exile to show that God's identity as Lord over Egypt remains constant, whether in salvation or judgment.
Exodus 6:6 provides the theological foundation for 'the outstretched hand' which is actually raised in Exodus 7:5 to demonstrate God's power over Egypt.
While 7:5 focuses on the Egyptians recognizing the Lord through judgment, 6:7 emphasizes that this is also the goal of Israel's deliverance.
Exodus 10:2 expands on the purpose of 'the signs' mentioned in 7:5 by showing that they also serve to teach future generations about God's power.
Ezekiel 30:8 uses the language of the Exodus judgments to show that God's identity as Lord over Egypt is manifested through both historical and prophetic judgments.
Ezekiel 20:42 shows the fulfillment of the promise that began in Exodus 7:5, where "to know the Lord" is the goal of the entire journey of salvation from Egypt to Canaan.
